newsitem.title: USA: Georgia gunman dies in 24-hour standoff with police.
newsitem.headline: Georgia gunman dies in 24-hour standoff with police.

text.p: A Georgia man was killed in a gun battle with police Saturday during a 24-hour standoff at his rural mobile home near Augusta, authorities said.

The gunman, identified as Wayne Miller of Lincoln County, wounded three police detectives in a 15-minute shootout just after 10 a.m. EST when Georgia Bureau of Investigation (GBI) agents tried to end a standoff that began Friday afternoon.

Police tried to negotiate with Miller through the night, but then lobbed tear-gas canisters into the mobile home. Miller opened fire with what appeared to be a shotgun and tossed out a hand grenade as law enforcement agents tried to rush the home.
The grenade did not explode, but three GBI agents were injured in the melee. They were treated at a hospital in nearby Augusta and released.
GBI spokeswoman Pamela Swanson said police opened fire after Miller threw out the grenade.

After the firefight, authorities waited for several hours without a further response from Miller. They then used a remote-controlled robot equipped with a camera to ensure that the scene was safe before entering the home and finding Miller dead.
Miller was described by police as a man in his late 40s who lived alone. Local media reports said the gunman's mother tried to help police talk him out.
The standoff began after state police and Lincoln County sheriff's deputies arrested another man Friday in an undercover drug bust that netted two to three pounds of marijuana.
A search of that suspect's home revealed another 30-35 pounds of marijuana and evidence that police said identified Miller as the source of the controlled substance.
Miller pulled a gun on GBI agents who went to his home to question him about the drug case. They took cover and the standoff ensued.
Lincolnton is located about 100 miles east of Atlanta.
